text:
Rasmus Ristolainen is back. The Flyers activated him off injured reserve on Nov 11, according to NHL.com and Pro Hockey Rumors, and he set up a goal that night in Edmonton; Broad Street Hockey called him "solid against Oilers". Three nights later he played 20.9 minutes in a win over Columbus.

Six games is far too few to judge, and the early five-on-five numbers are rough: Philadelphia has had 36.2% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 8 points worse than without him. We'd give that little weight yet. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 104th of 215 defensemen with 500-plus minutes, worth 0.5 wins above replacement, mostly from defense at even strength. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking backs that up: he stopped 15% of the entries aimed at him, against a typical 11%, so watch how often teams dump the puck in on his side rather than carry it. He also still has one of the hardest shots in the league, 98.23 mph, in the 98th percentile. At 32 and in his sixth season in Philadelphia, his job is to steady things.
headline: Ristolainen returns to a Flyers blue line that needs him
